newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO gird for battle over homes for Jews.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO gird for battle over homes for Jews.

text.p: Israelis and Palestinians girded for battle on Monday over the Jewish state's plan to build a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Israel reinforced troops in the West Bank and Gaza Strip to pre-empt Palestinian unrest when construction on the settlement begins in the coming days. Officials said they expected an Israel-PLO summit this week to defuse the spiralling tension.
Palestinian Authority member Faisal al-Husseini and about 15 other Palestinians launched a sit-in near the site slated for construction, pitching two tents and lighting a campfire.

"We decided we will have a tent here to watch what is going on the mountain. If they enter with their bulldozers, we will enter," Husseini, the PLO's official in charge of Jerusalem affairs, told reporters.
About 100 Israeli soldiers in full battle gear perched on a hill opposite Husseini's tents, armed with automotic rifles and tear gas grenades.

Bulldozers languished less than two kilometres (about a mile) away. Drivers said they were waiting for orders to start the work. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed on Sunday they would break ground this week.

Israel's decision this month to build 6,500 houses at the site angered Palestinians and plunged peace moves into a slump. Israeli officials insist peace agreements with the PLO do not bar settlement building.

Israeli security officials have warned the start of construction could spark violence. Clashes last September claimed the lives of 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers after Israel punched an opening in a tunnel in East Jerusalem near key Islamic sites.

"I ordered the deployment of forces starting today along a very wide perimeter in the Gaza Strip, the West Bank and along the seam (dividing Israel from the West Bank and Gaza)," said Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
"Our working assumption is that incidents are likely to occur, even severe incidents. For this reason we have deployed our forces," he told reporters.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said he expected a summit between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat would take place this week.

Israel, which captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East War, views it as part of its capital. Palestinians want that half of the city as the capital of a future state. Its future is supposed to be negotiated.
In Tel Aviv, Israel agreed at a meeting with Palestinian officials to allow Arafat to use an airport in Gaza for his personal flights.
The move was billed as an Israeli gesture to help ease the tension but Palestinians said the crisis would be defused only if Israel cancelled its settlement plans.
"The crisis is not centered on the issue of the president's airplane or the opening of the airport," said Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, general-secretary of the Palestinian Authority.
Israel handed over most of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank to Palestinian self-rule under peace deals since 1993 but retains overall control of security and border crossings.
The two sides have failed to reach an understanding that would allow Palestinians to open the airport in Gaza for commercial flights.
